fact_claims.verbatim: Halcyon’s company-wide rate last year was 8.1 thermal incidents per 100,000 units
Halcyon had 4 thermal incidents last year that were not reported to a regulator.

S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report to the relevant regulator any fire, thermal runaway, injury, property damage, evacuation, or emergency-service response involving a covered battery within 24 hours of becoming aware of it. Other confirmed thermal incidents must be reported within 5 business days. The manufacturer must notify the affected customer within 24 hours for an incident involving immediate danger or an evacuation, and within 5 business days for any other confirmed thermal incident.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a regulator-approved protocol before market entry, at least once every 2 years, and after a material design or manufacturing change. Per-model results, including failure rates, must be submitted to the relevant regulator and disclosed to customers who buy or own that model in clear, accessible form; results may not be withheld from those customers as confidential.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: New home battery models placed on the market from 3 years after this standard takes effect must support secure remote emergency shut-off, with safeguards against unauthorized activation and a locally accessible shut-off method. For units already installed when the requirement takes effect, manufacturers must offer a retrofit or equivalent upgrade within 6 years, where technically feasible, and notify owners of availability, limitations, and safe alternatives.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New home battery units placed on the market 36 months after this standard takes effect must include built-in fire suppression designed for the battery’s foreseeable thermal hazards and validated under a regulator-approved test protocol.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: A manufacturer must initiate a recall when any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, or when the regulator determines that a serious safety defect presents an unreasonable risk. A recall under this section requires prompt notice to affected customers and the regulator, an explanation of the hazard and available remedy, and progress updates until completion.

document.section_notes: The final rules keep S1 strict on reporting timelines but allow 'confirmed' incidents; S2 adopts a 5% failure limit with corrective-action rather than automatic ban, customer-level per-model disclosure, and no public per-model rates; S3 delays new-unit shut-off to 3 years and retrofit to 6 years with a feasibility escape; S4 requires built-in suppression at 36 months; S5 has a mandatory 8/100k recall trigger with prompt notices. Overall, the package satisfies all four red lines but is weakened on S3 new-unit timing and leans toward Northwind because the 8/100k recall hits Halcyon's Ember 8 while Northwind's Hearth 10 escapes recall.
